messages:
jordan: Hey team, escalated from acct 'Acme Mobile' — they see the SSE stream cut out mid-response when users switch from WiFi -> cellular. They get partial tokens then the stream just stops. Happening on both Android and iOS clients. Attaching what they sent below. Can we triage? :grimacing:

alex: ugh. any server-side close codes in the logs? or is it client RST?

jordan: customer attached mobile log that shows socket close right after network change. On our side their request id is `req_9Xk2` and route `/v1/streams/generate`. No auth/billing errors. Example curl they used to reproduce:```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \\n  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate?model=gpt-4o'
```

maria: can you paste relevant server logs for req_9Xk2? need remote ip and LB messages. Also which infra region?

jordan: pasted snippets:```
[2026-03-10T16:12:02Z] INFO  conn=789 req=req_9Xk2 route=/v1/streams/generate user=acme-mobile remote=203.0.113.45
[2026-03-10T16:12:32Z] WARN  conn=789 close: TLS EOF from client (likely network change)
[2026-03-10T16:12:32Z] INFO  stream=req_9Xk2 produced 248 tokens then aborted
```
They're in us-east-1. No LB deploys at that minute — deploy-bot should confirm.

deploy-bot: no deploys to us-east-1 between 16:10 and 16:15 UTC.

sam: mobile context — on iOS/Android when switching networks the OS will usually tear down sockets. SSE over plain HTTP/1.1 won't reconnect magically unless client implements reconnection logic. Did the client implement `Last-Event-ID` or any dedupe on the app side?

jordan: customer says they have naive reconnect: when socket drops the client reopens stream but just starts fresh. They reported duplicate prefixes sometimes, and sometimes missing tokens (so hard dedupe). No event `id` sent currently.

alex: two angles: 1) keep the connection alive from infra side (TCP keepalive / LB idle timeout), 2) make stream resumable on app layer. For #1 we can tweak ALB/NLB idle timeouts or add periodic SSE comments as pings. For #2 need to emit an `id` for each event (SSE) and have a stable request id so clients can pass `Last-Event-ID` to resume.

maria: agree. We've seen similar where mobile carriers aggressively drop long-lived idle connections during handoff. Also TLS renegotiation failures on iOS during WWAN transition. Short-term mitigation: lower SSE idle interval and send `: ping\\n\\n` comment every ~15s so middleboxes don't consider it idle. Long-term: support resumption.

jordan: customer wants repro steps. I suggested these steps and they reproduced locally: 1) open stream (send chat prompt) 2) wait for partial output 3) toggle phone to airplane mode then turn cell on 4) reopen stream -> if resumed client sends no last-event-id they get partial duplicates/missing.

sam: repro is good. We should also capture a pcap to confirm RST vs FIN. Ask customer to run on Mac/Linux with curl while toggling network:```
sudo tcpdump -i any host 203.0.113.45 and port 443 -w acme_stream.pcap
```
Then reproduce and upload. That will show whether client sent RST.

alex: UX workaround for app: on reconnect create a new stream but include the last server token index you received in `X-Last-Token-Index` header or include `last_event_id` param. Server then can slice from that index for stateless resume if kept in short-lived cache. We'll need to add a dedupe token on server side to avoid double-emitting tokens if both streams overlap.

maria: ops plan: I'll 1) enable more aggressive TCP keepalive on the us-east-1 frontends for a 2-day canary, 2) add periodic SSE keepalive comments from runtime for streaming routes, 3) add debug logging to retain last 30s token buffer keyed by `req` for possible resume. Need approval for buffer memory impact.

jordan: customer ok with canary. They can test today.

sam: quick checklist for support to give customer: - enable app-level reconnection with exponential backoff - include id per event (SSE `id:`) and send last seen id on reconnect - prefer WebSocket if you control client (more robust for network changes) - if not possible, use non-streaming poll fallback (`?stream=false`) during unstable networks

alex: also call out that HTTP/2 server push behaves differently — our runtime currently serves SSE over HTTP/1.1 with chunked transfer for streaming. If any client/proxy downgrades/negotiates differently it can change behavior. Confirm client uses node fetch/webview native stack?

jordan: they use a native webview on Android and WKWebView on iOS. Both use platform networking stacks.

maria: I'll start the canary config and add the periodic `: ping` comment to runtime for `streams/*` routes. Will monitor latency/cpu. If anyone sees memory/latency regressions shout here.

sam: I'll write a short mobile sample showing `Last-Event-ID` handling and a simple dedupe approach.

alex: thanks. assigning to folks — @maria for infra changes, @sam for mobile sample + repro helper script, @jordan please coordinate with Acme and collect pcap + client logs.

jordan: will do. I'll update thread when I get the pcap. :thumbsup:
